turns.query: Dumb question, but when I calibrate the acidity sensor can I just put it straight into the bottle the solution came in? Feels wasteful pouring it out every time.

relevant.evidence:
Do not insert an electrode or other material into a bottle
containing stock buffer solution
relevant.locator: Section 2.3 buffer precautions and section 3.0 / 3.1 Electrode Care and Cleaning — "Do not insert an electrode or other material into a bottle"

relevant.evidence:
Never pour used buffer back into a bottle containing the
stock buffer solution.
relevant.locator: Section 2.3 buffer precautions and Table 6.4–3 — "Values of pH from 0 to 90 degrees Celsius"

relevant.evidence:
label the bottle with the buffer’s pH value,
lot number, and expiration date.
relevant.locator: Section 4.0 calibration guidelines and section 4.1 Calibration Procedure — "Use at least two pH buffer solutions with documented, NIST-traceable pH values"

relevant.evidence:
Record the temperature and value of pH buffers used at
that temperature, with lot numbers and expiration dates,
in the pH-meter/electrode logbook.
relevant.locator: Section 4.1.1 steps 6-10 — "Begin calibration procedures" and the pour-swirl-discard rinse sequence
